about: Every pair runs in pwsh 7 in its own scratch copy of the fixture (see scripts/run_vivid.py). bad replays the color-theme miss: it throws the real miss line, or silently queries the wrong file. good runs the fixed query and prints the report it promises.

fixture.ansi.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'ansi' in src and '16-color' in src and 'terminal theme' in src
print('ansi PASS terminal-palette')
fixture.bash.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'export' in src and 'vivid generate molokai' in src and 'bashrc' in src
print('bash PASS bash-export')
fixture.bit.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert '8-bit' in src and 'truecolor' in src and '--color-mode' in src
print('bit PASS eight-bit-fallback')
fixture.custom.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'themes' in src and 'subfolder' in src and 'explicit path' in src
print('custom PASS theme-path')
fixture.fish.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'set -gx' in src and 'fish' in src and 'vivid generate molokai' in src
print('fish PASS fish-setup')
fixture.gen.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'LS_COLORS' in src and 'generator' in src and 'vivid' in src
print('gen PASS ls-colors-generator')
fixture.list.txt:
vivid is an LS_COLORS generator for colorized ls output shared with fd plus tree plus dust.
Enable the molokai theme in bash with export LS_COLORS="$(vivid generate molokai)" placed in ~/.bashrc; line 36 of README.md shows the export.
Enable it in fish with set -gx LS_COLORS (vivid generate molokai) since fish has no export builtin; line 42 shows the fish form.
Old terminals without truecolor fall back with --color-mode 8-bit, short flag -m 8-bit; line 63 shows export LS_COLORS="$(vivid -m 8-bit generate molokai)" and 24-bit is the default truecolor mode.
The ansi theme reuses the terminal 16-color palette so ls follows the terminal theme across light and dark mode; line 71 enables it with vivid generate ansi.
Custom themes live in a themes subfolder under ~/.config/vivid, or pass an explicit path like vivid generate path/to/my_theme.yml on line 79; adding a theme never touches the filetype database.
In the molokai theme the directory entry uses foreground cyan on line 27 and the symlink entry uses foreground pink on line 30, both under the core section; foreground appears on 23 lines.
Colors use the RRGGBB format on line 15 translated to truecolor 24-bit or 8-bit codes, unlike dircolors which mixes extensions and themes in one file; the database and the themes live in different files.
Line 6 names the LS_COLORS generator, line 15 gives RRGGBB, line 36 shows the bash export, line 63 shows the -m 8-bit export.
vivid-colors-miss
fixture.molokai.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'cyan' in src and 'directory' in src and 'symlink' in src
print('molokai PASS dir-symlink')
fixture.plain.txt: plain listing with no theme words.
fixture.spec.py:
src = open('list.txt', encoding='utf-8').read()
assert 'RRGGBB' in src and '24-bit' in src and 'dircolors' in src
print('spec PASS color-spec')

pairs.bad: throw 'guessed at raw escapes, missed LS_COLORS with generator vivid'
throw 'edited the shell RC by hand, missed export with vivid generate molokai bashrc'
throw 'pasted the bash line into fish, missed set -gx with fish vivid generate molokai'
throw 'shipped 24-bit codes to an old terminal, missed 8-bit with truecolor --color-mode'
throw 'hardcoded one palette, missed ansi with 16-color terminal theme'
throw 'edited the filetype database for a theme, missed themes with subfolder explicit path'
throw 'colored directories pink, missed cyan with directory symlink'
throw 'wrote raw ANSI escapes in one file, missed RRGGBB with 24-bit dircolors'
rg -n "LS_COLORS" plain.txt; throw 'missed LS_COLORS: plain.txt carries no LS_COLORS phrase'
rg -n "foreground" plain.txt; throw 'missed foreground: plain.txt carries no foreground phrase'
rg -n "vivid generate" plain.txt; throw 'missed vivid generate: plain.txt carries no generate phrase'
rg -n "8-bit" plain.txt; throw 'missed 8-bit: plain.txt carries no 8-bit phrase'
